content:
From: Alice Chan <alice.chan@tidebank.com>

Subject: TideBank: onramp connectivity options (peering / privatelink / s2s)

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our architecture team asked me to get a short, readable recommendation comparing three onramp patterns for a Private deployment of Redwood at TideBank: VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints), and site-to-site VPN (S2S).

Constraints to keep in mind:
- PCI scope: traffic to the inference cluster must not egress over the public internet once inside AWS.
- Multi-region DR: primary region in us-east-1, secondary in us-west-2.
- Mixed connectivity: some services are in our AWS accounts, others are in an on-prem DC (low-bandwidth replication links).
- Target P95 latency for inference: <60ms for our critical flows.

Can you provide a concise tradeoffs summary (latency, isolation, ops complexity, failover behavior, cost considerations) and outline a recommended pilot approach? I attached an internal topology diagram.

Attachments: tidebank-current-topology.pdf

Best,
Alice Chan
NetOps Lead — TideBank
alice.chan@tidebank.com

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: TideBank: onramp connectivity options (peering / privatelink / s2s)

Alice — thanks for the context and topology. Attaching a short matrix and a recommended pilot.

High level (TL;DR):
- If your traffic is strictly intra-AWS and low-latency, VPC Peering gives the lowest network RTT but requires account-level peering and cross-account routing work. Good for tight latency SLOs but adds management if you have many accounts.
- AWS PrivateLink provides strong isolation and keeps the endpoint private inside your VPC; it’s the cleanest from a security/PCI perspective because it avoids transitive routing across peering. Slightly higher per-request costs and a small latency delta.
- Site-to-site VPN is the simplest for on-prem connectivity and for customers who must keep a physical link, but it usually adds higher and variable latency and is less ideal for strict P95. Can be used as a fallback/DR leg.

Recommended pilot: (1) PrivateLink to a dedicated inference service endpoint in us-east-1 for PCI-scoped traffic; (2) parallel VPC peering trial for a small workload to measure delta; (3) S2S as a DR/fallback path to on-prem.

Next step: Ben will share a quick spreadsheet with expected latency/cost guidance and a sample rollout checklist. Can we do a 30-minute technical sync early next week?

—
Priya Natarajan
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

Subject: Re: TideBank: onramp connectivity options (peering / privatelink / s2s)

Adding some concrete tradeoffs and numbers from our side after a quick cost/latency model run. See attached Redwood_Onramp_Options.xlsx (tabbed: latency_estimates, cost_model, rollout_checklist).

Summary tradeoffs (quick):
- VPC Peering
  - Latency: best-case lowest RTT (we estimate ~5–15ms intra-AZ, 12–30ms cross-AZ/region depending on route). Good for P95 <60ms if everything in-region and paths are short.
  - Isolation: relies on IGW/NAT configs; peering does not provide interface-level isolation. ACLs/security groups are primary control.
  - Ops: Requires peering policy, route table changes, and potentially shared services; scaling to many accounts increases overhead.
  - Cost: low network data transfer cost inside region (often negligible vs PrivateLink per-GB charges).

- AWS PrivateLink (Interface Endpoints)
  - Latency: small added hop; typical additional 2–8ms vs peering depending on path. Still comfortably under 60ms for regional flows in most cases.
  - Isolation: strong — endpoint ENIs in your VPC, traffic never traverses public IPs. Aligns well with PCI scope.
  - Ops: Simpler from routing perspective (no cross-account route table management), but you pay for endpoint hours and per-GB data processed.
  - Cost: higher per-GB and hourly endpoint costs; easier to audit and to lock down with endpoint policies.

- Site-to-site VPN (S2S)
  - Latency: variable and higher (20–100ms+ depending on provider and last-mile). Not ideal for low-latency synchronous calls but useful for async/batch or administrative access.
  - Isolation: can be made compliant but often requires additional monitoring; depends on encryption/management.
  - Ops: Easier to set up for on-prem, but BGP/route churn and bandwidth constraints are operational factors.
  - Cost: lower to start, but may need dedicated circuits for predictable performance (MPLS/DX) which increases cost.

Suggested pilot plan (two-week sprint):
1) Provision PrivateLink endpoint in your us-east-1 VPC connected to a dedicated Redwood inference service (small fleet).
2) In parallel, create a peered VPC route (cross-account peering) for a single test account/workload to measure tail latency on matching traffic patterns.
3) Keep an S2S tunnel active to your on-prem lab as a failover path; run heavier batch and replication over that link.
4) Measure: token latency P50/P95/P999, egress data GB/day, operational tasks/time-to-rotate-keys.
5) Evaluate costs after 2 weeks; our spreadsheet includes a break-even point for PrivateLink vs peering based on GB/month.

Attachments: Redwood_Onramp_Options.xlsx

Happy to walk through the spreadsheet in the sync.
